players.product: power transformers and grid equipment buyer — US utility (largest HD Hyundai Electric customer)

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 adjusted EPS of $1.15; first-half adjusted EPS up 9.8% year-over-year. Energy Resources reported adjusted earnings growth of approximately 18% year-over-year, with contributions from new investments adding $0.09 per share, primarily reflecting continued growth in the power generation portfolio. FPL EPS rose $0.05 year-over-year on regulatory capital employed growth of approximately 9.3%.
quarterly_data.figure: adjusted EPS $1.15; 1H adjusted EPS +9.8% YoY; Energy Resources adjusted earnings +18% YoY; FPL regulatory capital employed +9.3%

quarterly_data.signal: 2026 adjusted EPS expectations range of $3.92 to $4.02 left unchanged, and the company is targeting the high end of that range. Adjusted EPS is expected to compound at 8% plus through 2032 with the same target from 2032 through 2035, all off the 2025 base of $3.71.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 adjusted EPS $3.92-$4.02 (targeting high end); 8%+ CAGR through 2032 and 2032-2035 off a $3.71 2025 base

quarterly_data.signal: Energy Resources added 3.6 gigawatts of renewables and storage to backlog, its second largest quarter of additions after last quarter's record 4 gigawatts; battery storage was 2 gigawatts of the additions. Backlog now totals approximately 35.1 gigawatts after 1.1 gigawatts of new projects were placed into service since the last call. The 2026-2029 backlog represents roughly two-thirds of development expectations midpoint through 2029, leaving about 18.6 gigawatts to add over roughly two years (management said this means doing about 9 gigawatts a year) to reach the midpoint.
quarterly_data.figure: backlog ~35.1 GW; +3.6 GW added in Q2 (2 GW battery storage); 1.1 GW placed in service; 18.6 GW still to add over ~2 years (~9 GW/yr)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO on equipment procurement: "we've proactively secured supply to support both FPL and Energy Resources development plans, including the development of our national data center hub footprint. For solar, we've secured panels through 2029. We're also well protected for battery storage with competitively priced domestic supply also secured through 2029. We have sufficient wind sites with expected federal permits to meet development expectations through 2029. And we have sufficient transformer capacity to support our build forecast through the end of the decade." Framed as planning for potential trade impacts. No equipment supplier was named on the call.
quarterly_data.figure: solar panels secured through 2029; domestic battery storage supply secured through 2029; wind sites/permits through 2029; transformer capacity secured through the end of the decade

quarterly_data.signal: FPL large load: expectations raised in May from 6 gigawatts to 8 gigawatts by 2032. Roughly 21 gigawatts of large load interest at FPL, of which 12 gigawatts is in advanced discussions, a portion of which could begin being served as soon as 2028. FPL continues to expect to announce at least one large load transaction under its tariff by the end of the year, and said it would not wait for a quarterly call to disclose it. Every gigawatt of large load under the approved tariff is expected to be equivalent to roughly $2 billion of capex earning the same ROE as other FPL investments. Florida's governor signed a bill in May codifying many aspects of FPL's large load tariff into law.
quarterly_data.figure: large load expectation raised 6 GW to 8 GW by 2032; ~21 GW of interest, 12 GW in advanced discussions; first service possible 2028; ~$2 billion of capex per GW

quarterly_data.signal: Data center hub strategy: 30 potential hubs now being discussed with the market, expected to rise to 40 by year-end. Four origination channels (direct with hyperscalers, investor-owned utilities, cooperative and municipal utilities, and federal partners) feed a base case of securing 15 gigawatts of new generation to serve large load by 2035, with an upside case of 30 gigawatts or more by 2035. Management described a bring-your-own-generation approach in front of or behind the meter, and said speed-to-power at a hub often starts with renewables (on the market in 12 to 18 months), then gas, then battery storage for behind-the-meter redundancy. No hyperscaler customer was named.
quarterly_data.figure: 30 hubs today rising to 40 by year-end; base case 15 GW of new generation for large load by 2035, upside 30 GW+; renewables deliverable in 12-18 months

quarterly_data.signal: Continuing to advance development of up to 9.5 gigawatts of gas-fired generation projects in Texas and Pennsylvania, drawn from the existing inventory of data center hubs; the President approved the projects in March. Definitive agreements with the U.S. and Japanese governments are still being negotiated and are running later than the two-to-three months indicated on the prior call, but Energy Resources said the expected in-service timing of those projects has not changed and development continues in the background while terms are worked out.
quarterly_data.figure: up to 9.5 GW of gas-fired generation in Texas and Pennsylvania; presidential approval March 2026; definitive agreements with U.S. and Japanese governments still pending; in-service timing unchanged

quarterly_data.signal: Nuclear: the Duane Arnold recommissioning remains on track to bring the plant back online no later than Q1 2029; since the last call the Iowa Utilities Commission approved a generating certificate for the plant and NextEra closed on the acquisition of the final 30% minority interest held by its two cooperative partners, making it the sole owner. On advanced nuclear, the company is evaluating the capabilities of various SMR OEMs (none named) and has 6 gigawatts of SMR co-location opportunities at its existing nuclear sites plus greenfield site development, but will only proceed under a structure with capped exposure and no cost-overrun risk, sharing risk across the developer, the customer/hyperscaler, the U.S. government, the OEM and an EPC contractor.
quarterly_data.figure: Duane Arnold restart no later than Q1 2029, final 30% minority interest acquired (now sole owner); 6 GW of SMR co-location opportunity at existing nuclear sites

quarterly_data.signal: Battery storage described as a key growth driver with four development routes: stand-alone projects, co-location at existing renewable sites, grid solutions, and expanding existing 4-hour batteries to 8 hours. The stand-alone and co-located battery storage pipeline sits at over 110 gigawatts, excluding those expansion opportunities. Management added that every gas-fired hub built to meet NERC requirements also needs a behind-the-meter storage reliability solution, making each hub an enabler for additional battery storage.
quarterly_data.figure: stand-alone and co-located battery storage pipeline over 110 GW (excludes 4-hour to 8-hour expansion opportunities)

quarterly_data.signal: FPL build-out: four new solar sites placed into service during the quarter, and FPL remains on track to meet full year expectations to install approximately 900 megawatts of solar and over 1.4 gigawatts of battery storage, continuing to own and operate more solar and storage than any utility in America. Roughly 90% of FPL's generation mix is anchored in baseload gas-fired and nuclear generation, which FPL said lets it integrate additional generation quickly for speed-to-market. FPL capital expenditures were approximately $2.8 billion in the quarter, with full year capital investments expected between $12 billion and $13 billion. FPL added more than 90,000 customers versus the prior year quarter; Q2 retail sales rose 0.4% (0.6% weather-normalized).
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 FPL install plan ~900 MW solar and over 1.4 GW battery storage; 4 solar sites in service in Q2; ~90% baseload gas and nuclear mix; FPL capex ~$2.8B in Q2 and $12 billion to $13 billion for the full year

capex.period: 2026 FPL plan (midpoint of the stated $12-13B range)

quarterly_data.signal: Recontracting of operating projects coming off contract: over 500 megawatts recontracted since the last earnings call, bringing the year-to-date total to over 1,100 megawatts of renewables. This quarter's recontractings were priced on average at a premium of roughly $20 per megawatt hour above recent realized pricing for those projects, with contracts locked in for approximately 15 years on average. Energy Resources has up to 6 gigawatts of renewables and 1.5 gigawatts of nuclear recontracting opportunities through 2032. CEO attributed the pricing to demand outrunning supply: "supply is not matching demand today, which is resulting in higher pricing across the board."
quarterly_data.figure: over 500 MW recontracted in the quarter, over 1,100 MW year-to-date, at ~$20 per MWh above recent realized pricing on ~15-year terms; up to 6 GW renewables and 1.5 GW nuclear recontracting opportunity through 2032

quarterly_data.signal: NextEra Energy Transmission energized a 137-mile, 345 kV line in New Mexico ahead of schedule and on budget, 31 months from award to in-service, projected by a Southwest Power Pool study to cut typical residential bills by about $13 per month in 2031. MISO also selected NextEra Energy Transmission as part of a consortium to develop two large-scale 765 kV transmission projects in Illinois; NextEra Energy Transmission would hold 43% ownership of the approximately $1.6 billion project, intended as a backbone system for the Midwest. Management said the transmission business, electric and gas jointly, is moving from mid-single-digit to 20s growth.
quarterly_data.figure: 137-mile 345 kV New Mexico line energized in 31 months (~$13/month bill reduction in 2031); MISO awarded two 765 kV Illinois projects, ~$1.6 billion with 43% NextEra Energy Transmission ownership

quarterly_data.signal: Pending combination with Dominion Energy advancing: merger applications filed July 15 with the Virginia State Corporation Commission, North Carolina Utilities Commission and South Carolina Public Service Commission (starting Virginia's six-month statutory review), plus FERC and NRC filings, and an S-4 filed July 9 that became effective the day before this call. Closing is still expected in the second half of 2027. The offer includes $2.25 billion of shareholder-funded bill credits for Dominion customers. The combined company is expected to support approximately 11% annual growth in regulatory capital employed through 2032 and 9% plus adjusted EPS growth through 2032 and 2035 off a 2025 base, and management expects to more than double the size of the combined company by 2032, which it framed as economic development for OEMs and EPC contractors serving its build.
quarterly_data.figure: merger filings made July 15 (VA/NC/SC) plus FERC and NRC; $2.25 billion of bill credits; combined company ~11% annual regulatory capital employed growth and 9%+ adjusted EPS growth through 2032; close expected 2H 2027
quarterly_data.counterparty_role: merger target (pending combination, not a supply relationship)
